Looking at the code, I need to analyze the `Prove` lemma in `HelperA.dfy` and fix its proof body.

The lemma states:
- Requires: `K.Clean(s)`
- Ensures: `K.Compress(s) == s`

The current proof has an issue. When `|s| >= 2`, we need to:
1. Establish that `K.Clean(s[1..])` holds (using `O.TailInvariant`)
2. Recursively prove for the tail
3. Show the boundary condition and keep case

Let me trace through the logic:
- `O.TailInvariant(s)` - proves `K.Clean(s[1..])` when `K.Clean(s) && 2 <= |s|`
- `O.Boundary(s)` - proves `s[0] != s[1]` when `K.Clean(s) && 2 <= |s|`
- `O.Keep(s)` - proves `K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + K.Compress(s[1..])` when `2 <= |s| && s[0] != s[1]`

The recursive call `Prove(s[1..])` requires `K.Clean(s[1..])`, so I need to call `O.TailInvariant(s)` before the recursive call.

After the recursive call establishes `K.Compress(s[1..]) == s[1..]`, and `O.Keep(s)` establishes `K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + K.Compress(s[1..])`, we can conclude `K.Compress(s) == [s[0]] + s[1..] == s`.

Here's the corrected proof:

```json
{"HelperA.dfy": "if |s| < 2 {\n      O.Base(s);\n    } else {\n      O.TailInvariant(s);\n      Prove(s[1..]);\n      O.Boundary(s);\n      O.Keep(s);\n      assert s == [s[0]] + s[1..];\n    }"}
```
